title: Ant Colony Life Cycle
script: Ants live together in colonies, which are eusocial, communal, and efficiently organized. A typical colony consists of one or more egg-laying queens, numerous sterile females, and seasonally, many winged sexual males and females. According to Wikipedia, ants undertake flights to establish new colonies, with swarms of winged sexuals departing the nest in search of other nests. The males die shortly thereafter, while a small percentage of females survive to initiate new nests. As superorganisms, ant colonies operate with a unified purpose, with each caste playing a vital role in the colony's survival. With over 13,800 described species, ants have colonized almost every landmass on Earth, thriving in moist tropical ecosystems and exceeding the combined biomass of wild birds and mammals in some regions, as noted in the Journal of Insect Science.
